_about: Paynora, a fictional Indian HRMS and payroll product. The ONE source of brand, modules, plans and tax rules for both demos (payroll_site and payroll_app). Hand-authored; build_data.py copies it to demos/payroll_site/data/product.json and the e2e tests fail if the copy drifts. Every company, person and number here is invented.

tax._about: Indian income tax on salary for ONE stated year, read by the Python engine (payroll_app/backend/payroll_engine.py) and its TypeScript twin. Well-established rules only; the demos call it illustrative.
tax.disclaimer: Illustrative calculation for FY 2025-26 under the Income-tax Act, 1961, for a resident individual below 60 with salary income only. Not tax advice.
tax.rounding: Total income rounded to the nearest ₹10 (section 288A); tax payable rounded to the nearest ₹10 (section 288B).
tax.surcharge_note: Surcharge applies only above ₹50 lakh of income. Every sample employee is below that, so none is shown.

hra.rule: Exempt HRA is the least of: HRA received; rent paid minus 10% of basic; 50% of basic in Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata or Chennai, 40% elsewhere.

lta.rule: Leave travel allowance is exempt up to the actual fare for travel within India, for two journeys in a block of four calendar years. Old regime only.

sections.80C: Investments and payments such as EPF (employee share), PPF, ELSS, life insurance premium, children's tuition fees and home-loan principal, up to ₹1,50,000 in all.
sections.80CCD1B: Your own NPS contribution, up to ₹50,000, over and above 80C.
sections.80D: Health insurance premium: up to ₹25,000 for self, spouse and children (₹50,000 if you are a senior citizen), and up to ₹25,000 more for parents (₹50,000 if they are senior citizens). Preventive check-ups up to ₹5,000 count within these limits.
sections.24b: Interest on a home loan for a self-occupied house, up to ₹2,00,000.
sections.hra: House rent allowance exemption for rent you pay. A landlord's PAN is needed when rent is above ₹1,00,000 a year.
sections.lta: Leave travel allowance for domestic travel, on the actual fare.
sections.standard_deduction: A flat deduction from salary: ₹75,000 in the new regime, ₹50,000 in the old.
sections.professional_tax: State professional tax deducted from salary, up to ₹2,500 a year. Old regime only.
sections.87A: A rebate that brings tax to nil when total income is up to ₹12,00,000 in the new regime (rebate up to ₹60,000, with marginal relief just above) or ₹5,00,000 in the old regime (up to ₹12,500).
sections.tds: TDS on salary (section 192): the employer estimates the year's tax and deducts it evenly over the months left, recalculating every month as salary, leave or declarations change.
sections.form16: Form 16 is the certificate of TDS on salary. Part A lists the tax deducted and deposited; Part B shows how salary, exemptions and deductions add up to the tax. Employers issue it by 15 June after the year ends.

tax.regime_choice: An employee tells the employer which regime to use for TDS at the start of the year; without a choice, the new regime applies. The final choice is made in the income-tax return.

pf.note: 12% of basic each from employee and employer, here on basic capped at the ₹15,000 wage ceiling.

esi.note: Applies when monthly gross is up to ₹21,000. Contributions rounded up to the next rupee.

professional_tax.note: Illustrative state slabs on monthly gross salary for FY 2025-26.
